newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Pertamina to shut Balikpapan refinery.
newsitem.headline: Pertamina to shut Balikpapan refinery.

text.p: Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina will shut down its 200,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) Balikpapan refinery for four weeks from July 10 for routine maintenance, a Pertamina official said on Wednesday.

"Yes, we will shut the 200,000 bpd crude distillation unit of the Balikpapan refinery from tomorrow (July 10) for four weeks for maintenance. This is routine," Samto Utomo, Pertamina junior processing director, told Reuters.
"There will be no problems with fuel products supply in the country. We hope the shutdown will not be as long as scheduled," he added.
He said one of the two 22,500-bpd hydrocrackers at the refinery will continue to operate while the other one will be shut down. He gave no other details.
Pertamina has two refineries in Balikpapan. The second has a capacity of 50,000 bpd. A third, with a capacity of 65,000 bpd, will start up in August.
